sentences.chinese: 上不象賢，下不議功，而是非雜糅，例受茅土。
sentences.literal: Those above do not model themselves on the worthy; those below do not have merit weighed; yet right and wrong are tangled together, and by precedent all alike receive feudal soil.
sentences.idiomatic: The throne mirrors no sage; the ranks earn no fair tally of deeds—yet rumor and truth are stirred into one pot, and everyone walks away clutching a slice of realm.

sentences.chinese: 似權時之宜，非經久之制，將遂不改，此亦煩擾之人，漸亂之階也。
sentences.literal: It resembles what suits a moment of expediency; it is not a lasting system; should it then be followed without change, this too is for troubled folk the gradual stairway of disorder.
sentences.idiomatic: It answers the panic of the hour, not the architecture of generations; let it harden uncorrected and you hand troublemakers the bottom step toward ruin.

sentences.chinese: 夫國之興也，由於九族親睦，黎庶協和；
sentences.literal: Now in the rise of a state: it comes from the nine kindreds being intimate and harmonious, and the black-haired multitude being concordant.
sentences.idiomatic: Realms climb when kin rings true and the common people breathe as one lung.

sentences.chinese: 其衰也，在於骨肉疏絕，百姓離心。
sentences.literal: In its decline: it lies in flesh and bone growing estranged and cut off, and the hundred surnames losing heart.
sentences.idiomatic: They fall when blood thins to strangers and the crowd turns its face away.

sentences.chinese: 故夏邦不安，伊尹歸殷；
sentences.literal: Therefore when the Xia domain was not secure, Yi Yin returned to Yin.
sentences.idiomatic: So when Xia shook apart, Yi Yin crossed home to Yin.

sentences.chinese: 殷邦不和，呂氏入周。
sentences.literal: When the Yin domain was not harmonious, the house of Lü entered Zhou.
sentences.idiomatic: When Yin quarreled with itself, the Lü came west to Zhou.

sentences.chinese: 殷監在於夏後，去事之誡，誠來事之鑒也。
sentences.literal: Yin's mirror stands after Xia; the warning drawn from what has gone is truly the mirror for what will come.
sentences.idiomatic: Shang learned staring at Xia's corpse; yesterday's lecture is tomorrow's lantern.

sentences.chinese: 又陳曰：
sentences.literal: Again he presented and said:
sentences.idiomatic: He pressed on:

sentences.chinese: 昔伐蜀，募取涼州兵馬、羌胡健兒，許以重報，五千餘人，隨艾討賊，功皆第一。
sentences.literal: Formerly in attacking Shu they recruited Liangzhou troops and horses, Qiang and Hu stalwarts, promising heavy reward; more than five thousand followed Deng Ai to punish the rebels, and their merit was in every case of the first grade.
sentences.idiomatic: When Shu fell, Liangzhou riders and lean Qiang and Hu fighters were sworn thick pay; five thousand marched with Deng Ai, and each brought home the highest tally on the scroll.

sentences.chinese: 而《乙亥詔書》，州郡將督，不與中外軍同，雖在上功，無應封者。
sentences.literal: Yet in the edict of the Yihai year, commandery and prefecture generals and supervisors were not treated the same as inner and outer armies; though they bore upper merit, there were none who matched criteria for enfeoffment.
sentences.idiomatic: But the Yihai edict denied provincial captains parity with palace hosts and field armies—even deeds stamped "first class" won no patent of nobility.

sentences.chinese: 唯金城太守楊欣所領兵，以逼江由之勢，得封者三十人。
sentences.literal: Only the troops led by Jincheng Administrator Yang Xin, by the circumstance of pressing Jiangyou, had thirty who obtained enfeoffment.
sentences.idiomatic: Only Yang Xin's Jincheng column, pinning Jiangyou by the throat, saw thirty men raised to rank.

sentences.chinese: 自金城以西，非在欣部，無一人封者。
sentences.literal: From west of Jincheng, those not in Xin's division—not one was enfeoffed.
sentences.idiomatic: West of Jincheng, outside Yang Xin's roster, not one soldier tasted title.

sentences.chinese: 苟在中軍之例，雖下功必侯；
sentences.literal: If they fell under central-army precedent, though merit was lower they would surely be marquises;
sentences.idiomatic: Serve by central-army rule and modest stripes still bought a marquis's seal;

sentences.chinese: 如在州郡，雖功高不封，非所謂近不重施，遠不遺恩之謂也。
sentences.literal: if they were in commanderies and prefectures, though merit was high they were not enfeoffed—this is not what is called "near not doubling favors, far not leaving kindness aside."
sentences.idiomatic: hold a provincial posting and towering deeds meant silence—hardly the old pledge that reward need not pile up near the throne while distant sweat is still remembered.

sentences.chinese: 臣聞魚懸由於甘餌，勇夫死於重報。
sentences.literal: Your subject has heard that fish hang because of sweet bait, and brave men die on account of heavy reward.
sentences.idiomatic: Sweet bait lifts fish from the stream; heavy coin buys the brave man's last breath.

sentences.chinese: 故荊軻慕燕丹之義，專諸感闔閭之愛，匕首振于秦庭，吳刀耀於魚腹，視死如歸，豈不有由也哉！
sentences.literal: Therefore Jing Ke admired the righteousness of Crown Prince Dan of Yan; Zhuan Zhu was stirred by Helü's kindness—the dagger gleamed in Qin's court, the Wu blade flashed from the fish's belly; they regarded death as returning home—was there not cause!
sentences.idiomatic: So Jing Ke rode Yan Dan's honor and Zhuan Zhu answered Helü's favor—steel shocked the Qin hall, a blade leapt from the banquet fish—and both stepped toward death as toward their own hearth. Of course they did.

sentences.chinese: 夫功名重賞，士之所競，不平致怨，由來久矣。
sentences.literal: Now fame, merit, and heavy reward are what gentlemen contend for; injustice bringing resentment has been long standing.
sentences.idiomatic: Glory and gold are what fighting spirits chase; grudges born of unfair scales are older than memory.

sentences.chinese: 《詩》云：「屍鳩在桑，其子七兮。
sentences.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "The turtle dove on the mulberry—its chicks are seven.
sentences.idiomatic: The Songs record: "On the mulberry sits the shijiu—seven chicks beneath her wing.

sentences.chinese: 淑人君子，其儀一兮。
sentences.literal: The good man, the gentleman—his bearing is one."
sentences.idiomatic: The worthy man's measure never divides."

sentences.chinese: 」臣以為此等宜蒙爵封。
sentences.literal: " Your subject considers that men of this sort ought to receive noble rank and enfeoffment.
sentences.idiomatic: " Men of that stamp deserve patents and fields—I would see them clothed in both.

sentences.chinese: 灼前後陳事，輒見省覽。
sentences.literal: Zhuo, presenting affairs before and after, was always granted review and reading.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhuo memorialized again and again—and each time the throne looked.

sentences.chinese: 然身微宦孤，不見進序，乃取長假還鄉里。
sentences.literal: Yet his person was lowly and his office solitary; he saw no advancement in sequence; therefore he took extended leave and returned to his village.
sentences.idiomatic: Lowborn and alone in rank, he gained no step forward—so he claimed long leave and walked home.

sentences.chinese: 臨去，遣息上表曰：
sentences.literal: On the verge of going, he sent his son to submit a memorial saying:
sentences.idiomatic: Before he went, he had his son lay this plea before you:

sentences.chinese: 臣受恩三世，剖符守境，試用無績，沈伏數年，犬馬之力，無所復堪。
sentences.literal: Your subject has received grace through three reigns, split tallies and guarded borders; tried in office without achievement, sunk low several years; the strength of dog and horse has nothing further it can bear.
sentences.idiomatic: Three reigns have clothed me in favor; I bore tally and march yet proved hollow; years vanished in the shadows—this old hound has no stride left.

sentences.chinese: 陛下弘廣納之聽，采狂夫之言，原臣侵官之罪，不問幹忤之愆，天地恩厚，於臣足矣。
sentences.literal: Your Majesty broadly opens receptive hearing, adopts a madman's words, forgives your subject's crime of encroaching on office, does not inquire into the fault of blunt offense; Heaven and Earth are thick in kindness—for your subject it is enough.
sentences.idiomatic: Your Majesty hears wide enough to heed a crank, forgave my overreach, and never punished blunt speech—such heaven-high mercy leaves me full.

sentences.chinese: 臣聞忠臣之于其君，猶孝子之於其親：進則有欣然之慶，非貪官也；
sentences.literal: Your subject has heard that the loyal minister toward his lord is like the filial son toward his parents: in advancing there is glad rejoicing—it is not greed for office;
sentences.idiomatic: They say the faithful servant loves his lord as a dutiful son loves his parents: promotion sparks joy—not hunger for title;

sentences.chinese: 退則有戚然之憂，非懷祿也。
sentences.literal: in retiring there is sorrowful worry—it is not cherishing stipend.
sentences.idiomatic: withdrawal brings ache—not clutching salary.

sentences.chinese: 其意在於不忘光君榮親，情所不能已已者也。
sentences.literal: The intention lies in not forgetting to brighten the lord and honor kin—it is what emotion cannot cease ceasing.
sentences.idiomatic: The aim is only to lend luster to sovereign and kin—a longing that will not quiet.

sentences.chinese: 臣伏自悼，私懷至恨：生長荒裔，而久在外任，自還抱疾，未嘗覲見，陛下竟不知臣何人，此臣之恨一也。
sentences.literal: Your subject prostrates himself and mourns himself, privately harboring utmost regret: born and raised on a remote frontier, long assigned abroad; since returning bearing illness, never having had audience—Your Majesty still does not know who your subject is—this is regret one for your subject.
sentences.idiomatic: I kneel in private grief nursing five wounds: raised beyond the rim, long posted far—since sickness drove me home I have never looked into your eyes; you barely know my name—that is my first regret.

sentences.chinese: 遭運會之世，值有事之時，而不能垂功名於竹帛，此臣之恨二也。
sentences.literal: Encountering an age of shifting fortune, meeting a time of affairs, yet unable to hang fame and merit on bamboo and silk—this is regret two for your subject.
sentences.idiomatic: I drew breath in an age that shook yet left no brushstroke for me—that is my second regret.

sentences.chinese: 逮事聖明之君，而尪悴羸劣，陳力又不能，當歸死於地下，此臣之恨三也。
sentences.literal: Having reached service under a sage-bright lord, yet wizened, wasted, weak and inferior, unable to display strength—properly one should return and die underground—this is regret three for your subject.
sentences.idiomatic: I finally serve a luminous sovereign too broken to lift my weight—I belong under the clay—that is my third regret.

sentences.chinese: 哀二親早亡隕，兄弟並凋喪，孝敬無復施於家門，此臣之恨四也。
sentences.literal: Grieving that both parents died young and fell; brothers together withered and perished; filial respect has nowhere further to be practiced at the gate—this is regret four for your subject.
sentences.idiomatic: Parents fell early; brothers followed—I have no porch left for duty—that is my fourth regret.

sentences.chinese: 夏之日忽以過，冬之夜尋復來，人生百歲，尚以為不足，而臣中年嬰災，此臣之恨五也。
sentences.literal: Summer's days suddenly pass; winter's nights soon come again; human life a hundred years still deemed insufficient—yet your subject in middle years encountered calamity—this is regret five for your subject.
sentences.idiomatic: Summer races off; winter nights circle back; even a century feels brief—yet disaster caught me midlife—that is my fifth regret.

sentences.chinese: 慚日月之所養，愧昊蒼而無報，此臣之所以懷五恨而歎息，臨歸路而自悼者也。
sentences.literal: Ashamed before what sun and moon nurture, shamed before vast azure without repayment—this is why your subject harbors five regrets and sighs, facing the road home and mourning himself.
sentences.idiomatic: I blush before what sun and moon fed me and cannot repay the sky—so I nurse five sighs on the road toward home.

sentences.chinese: 語有之曰：「華言虛也，至言實也，苦言藥也，甘言疾也。
sentences.literal: A saying has it: "Ornate words are empty; utmost words are substance; bitter words are medicine; sweet words are sickness.
sentences.idiomatic: The proverb runs: "Silken speech is hollow; plain truth weighs solid; bitter counsel cures; honeyed flattery sickens.

sentences.chinese: 」臣欲言天下太平，而靈龜神狐未見，仙芝萐莆未生，麒麟未遊乎靈禽之囿，鳳皇未儀於太極之庭，此臣之所以不敢華言而為佞者也。
sentences.literal: " Your subject wishes to speak that All Under Heaven is greatly pacified, yet spirit tortoise and divine fox have not appeared, immortal zhi and auspicious shapu have not sprouted, qilin has not roamed the garden of numinous birds, phoenix has not displayed deportment in the Grand Ultimate court—this is why your subject dare not speak ornate words and become a flatterer.
sentences.idiomatic: " I long to cry "All is peace!"—yet no sacred tortoise or silver fox appears, no lucky fungi break soil, no qilin paces the royal aviary, no phoenix patterns the palace yard—so I refuse to varnish truth.

sentences.chinese: 昔漢高祖初定天下，于時戍卒婁敬上書諫曰：「陛下取天下不與成周同，而欲比靈斯成周，臣竊以為不侔。
sentences.literal: Formerly when Han Gaozu first settled All Under Heaven, at that time garrison soldier Lou Jing submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "Your Majesty's taking All Under Heaven is not the same as accomplished Zhou's; yet desiring to compare sacred fortune with accomplished Zhou, your subject privately thinks they do not match.
sentences.idiomatic: When Gaozu first steadied the realm, the conscript Lou Jing warned: "You won the empire unlike the perfected Zhou—yet you mean to match their divine heyday; I cannot see the likeness.

sentences.chinese: 」於是漢祖感悟，深納其言，賜姓為劉氏。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon Han's ancestor was moved to insight, deeply accepted his words, and granted him the surname Liu.
sentences.idiomatic: " The Han founder listened hard, took the lesson in full, and folded Lou Jing into the imperial clan.

sentences.chinese: 又顧謂陸賈曰：「為我著秦所以亡，而吾所以得之者。
sentences.literal: Again he turned and said to Lu Jia: "For me write why Qin thus perished, and why I thus obtained it.
sentences.idiomatic: He turned to Lu Jia: "Set down how Qin fell and how I rose.

sentences.chinese: 」賈乃作《新語》之書，述敘前世成敗，以為勸戒。
sentences.literal: " Jia then composed the book New Discourses, narrating former generations' success and failure, as admonition and warning.
sentences.idiomatic: " Lu Jia answered with his New Discourses, threading old victories and collapses into mirror and caution.

sentences.chinese: 又田肯建一言之計，非親子弟莫可使王齊者，而受千金之賜。
sentences.literal: Again Tian Ken proposed a plan of one sentence: none but intimate sons and younger brothers should be made kings of Qi—and received a gift of a thousand in gold.
sentences.idiomatic: Tian Ken earned a fortune of gold with one sentence—only royal kin should rule Qi.

sentences.chinese: 故世稱漢祖之寬明博納，所以能成帝業也。
sentences.literal: Therefore the age praises Han Progenitor's breadth, clarity, and broad acceptance—thereby he was able to accomplish imperial enterprise.
sentences.idiomatic: Hence men sing of Gaozu's wide mind—that was how he hammered out an empire.

sentences.chinese: 今之言世者，皆曰堯舜復興，天下已太平矣。
sentences.literal: Now those who speak of the age all say Yao and Shun have revived and All Under Heaven is already greatly pacified.
sentences.idiomatic: Today's chorus insists Yao and Shun walk again and the realm already sleeps in calm.

sentences.chinese: 臣獨以為未，亦竊有所勸焉。
sentences.literal: Your subject alone considers it not yet so, and also privately has something to urge.
sentences.idiomatic: I alone say "not yet"—and beg leave to push one counsel.

sentences.chinese: 且百王垂制，聖賢吐言，來事之明鑒也。
sentences.literal: Moreover the hundred kings' suspended systems, sages and worthies' uttered words are bright mirrors for affairs to come.
sentences.idiomatic: Besides, the statutes kings left and phrases sages breathed out are lanterns for what follows.

sentences.chinese: 孟子曰：「堯不能以天下與舜，則舜之有天下也，天與之也。
sentences.literal: Mencius said: "If Yao could not give All Under Heaven to Shun, then Shun's possessing All Under Heaven was Heaven giving it to him.
sentences.idiomatic: Mencius wrote: "If Yao could not hand the realm to Shun, then Shun's throne was Heaven's gift.

sentences.chinese: 昔舜為相，堯崩，三年之喪畢，舜避堯之子于南河，天下諸侯朝覲者、獄訟者，不之堯之子而之舜。
sentences.literal: Formerly when Shun was minister, Yao died; when the three years' mourning ended, Shun yielded place to Yao's son at South River; of All Under Heaven's feudal lords who came to audience or brought lawsuits, none went to Yao's son but went to Shun.
sentences.idiomatic: Once Shun served as minister: Yao died; mourning ended; Shun withdrew south of the river before Yao's heir—yet every lord who sought judgment chose Shun's tent, not the boy's.

sentences.chinese: 舜曰天也，乃之中國，踐天子位焉。
sentences.literal: Shun said it was Heaven; then he went to the central domains and ascended the Son of Heaven's position.
sentences.idiomatic: Shun called it Heaven's nod, entered the heartland, and mounted the throne.

sentences.chinese: 若居堯之宮，逼堯之子，非天所與者也。
sentences.literal: If one dwelt in Yao's palace and pressed Yao's son, that would not be what Heaven granted.
sentences.idiomatic: Occupy Yao's halls and shoulder his heir aside—that is no heavenly mandate.

sentences.chinese: 」曩昔西有不臣之蜀，東有僭號之吳，三主鼎足，並稱天子。
sentences.literal: " Formerly to the west was Shu that did not submit as subject; to the east was Wu that usurped titles; three lords stood tripod-footed, together calling themselves Son of Heaven.
sentences.idiomatic: " Once Shu in the west refused fealty; Wu in the east stole regalia—three kings balanced like tripod legs, each crying "Son of Heaven."

sentences.chinese: 魏文帝率萬乘之眾，受禪於靡陂，而自以德同唐、虞，以為漢獻即是古之堯，自謂即是今之舜，乃謂孟柯、孫卿不通禪代之變，遂作禪代之文，刻石垂戒，班示天下，傳之後世，亦安能使將來君子皆曉然心服其義乎！
sentences.literal: Wei Wendi led hosts of ten thousand chariots, received abdication at Mobei, and deemed his virtue matched Tang and Yu; he thought Emperor Xian was the Yao of antiquity and himself was the Shun of today—thereupon pronounced Meng Ke and Sun Qing ignorant of the changes of abdication succession; then composed texts on abdication succession, carved them in stone as hanging warning, promulgated display under Heaven, transmitted them to later ages—how could that ever make gentlemen yet to come all plainly understand in heart and submit to its righteousness!
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei marched ten thousand chariots to Mobei for the abdication yet fancied himself Tang or Yu—Han Xiandi his ancient Yao, himself the modern Shun—then mocked Mencius and Xunzi for missing the ritual arithmetic of yielding thrones, etched sermons in stone, and mailed them to posterity—could that truly bend tomorrow's gentlemen to conviction?

sentences.chinese: 然魏文徒希慕堯、舜之名，推新集之魏，欲以同于唐、虞之盛，忽骨肉之恩，忘籓屏之固，竟不能使四海賓服，混一皇化，而于時群臣莫有諫者，不其過矣哉！
sentences.literal: Yet Wei Wen vainly yearned after Yao and Shun's names, promoted the newly gathered Wei, desired to align with Tang and Yu's splendor, neglected flesh-and-bone kindness, forgot screen-barrier solidity—ultimately could not make the four seas guest-submit and merge in imperial transformation—yet at that time among assembled ministers none remonstrated—is it not excessive fault!
sentences.idiomatic: Yet Wendi chased Yao-Shun glitter while hoisting young Wei, dreamed of Tang-Yu zeniths, shrugged off kin and frontier walls—never bent the four seas to one awe—and still no minister dared cough a warning: what failure was that?

sentences.chinese: 孫卿曰：「堯、舜禪讓，是不然矣。
sentences.literal: Sun Qing said: "Yao and Shun's yielding abdication—is not so.
sentences.idiomatic: Xunzi objected: "That fairy tale about Yao yielding to Shun—no.

sentences.chinese: 天下者，至重也，非至強莫之能任；
sentences.literal: All Under Heaven is utmost heavy—not utmost strong and none can bear it;
sentences.idiomatic: The realm weighs absolute—without supreme strength no shoulders lift it;

sentences.chinese: 至大也，非至辯莫之能分；
sentences.literal: utmost great—not utmost eloquent and none can divide it;
sentences.idiomatic: it spans absolute breadth—without supreme discernment no mind maps it;

sentences.chinese: 至眾也，非至明莫之能見。
sentences.literal: utmost numerous—not utmost clear-sighted and none can see it.
sentences.idiomatic: it teems beyond counting—without luminous judgment no eye masters it.

sentences.chinese: 此三至者，非聖人莫之能盡。
sentences.literal: These three ultimates—not a sage and none can exhaust them.
sentences.idiomatic: Those three peaks only a sage can summit.

sentences.chinese: 」由此言之，孫卿、孟軻亦各有所不取焉。
sentences.literal: " From this speaking, Sun Qing and Meng Ke also each have what they do not accept.
sentences.idiomatic: " Even Xunzi and Mencius carved chunks from each other's creed.

sentences.chinese: 陛下受禪，從東府入西宮，兵刃耀天，旌旗翳日。
sentences.literal: Your Majesty received abdication, went from Eastern Offices into Western Palace; weapons glittered to Heaven, banners shaded the sun.
sentences.idiomatic: Your own succession ran from Eastern Annex to Western Palace—blade-light stabbed the sky, banners swallowed the sun.

sentences.chinese: 雖應天順人，同符唐、虞，然法度損益，則亦不異于昔魏文矣，故宜資三至以強制之。
sentences.literal: Although answering Heaven and obeying people, matching tally with Tang and Yu, yet in laws and measures decrease-increase then also not different from former Wei Wen—therefore it is fitting to rely on the three ultimates to strengthen and restrain it.
sentences.idiomatic: You answered Heaven and men like Tang and Yu—yet the tweaks of statute echo Wei Wendi's handbook—so lean on those three ultimates and bolt the gate.

sentences.chinese: 而今諸王有立國之名，而無襟帶之實。
sentences.literal: Now the various kings have the name of establishing states, yet lack the substance of lapel-and-girdle terrain.
sentences.idiomatic: Today princes wear kingdoms on paper yet hold no strategic belt of land.

sentences.chinese: 又蜀地有自然之險，是曆世奸雄之所窺覦，逋逃之所聚也，而無親戚子弟之守，此豈深思遠慮，杜漸防萌者乎！
sentences.literal: Moreover Shu territory has natural peril; it is what successive ages' crafty heroes covertly covet and where fugitives gather—yet there are no kin or sons and younger brothers guarding it—is this how one deeply thinks far plans, stops gradual onset and guards sprouts!
sentences.idiomatic: Shu's cliffs tempt every schemer and shelter every outlaw—yet no royal cousins stand watch there: is that how wise men stamp sparks before they bloom?

sentences.chinese: 昔漢文帝據已成之業，六合同風，天下一家。
sentences.literal: Formerly Han Wendi occupied already accomplished enterprise; six directions shared one wind; All Under Heaven one family.
sentences.idiomatic: Han Wendi inherited a finished realm—every quarter breathed one wind, the map one hearth.

sentences.chinese: 而賈誼上疏陳當時之勢，猶以為譬如抱火厝於積薪之下，而寢其上，火未及然，因謂之安。
sentences.literal: Yet Jia Yi submitted memorial stating the age's situation, still thinking it like embracing fire placed under piled kindling and sleeping atop it; fire had not yet burned—thereupon calling it secure.
sentences.idiomatic: Still Jia Yi warned the throne was sleeping on stacked kindling with live coals tucked beneath—flames not yet licking—yet ministers called it safe.

sentences.chinese: 此言誠存不忘亡，安不忘亂者也。
sentences.literal: These words truly are preserving existence not forgetting perishing, in peace not forgetting chaos.
sentences.idiomatic: That voice is the discipline of remembering ruin while you breathe and storm while you dine.

sentences.chinese: 然臣之慺慺，亦竊願陛下居安思危，無曰高高在上，常念臨深之義，不忘履冰之戒。
sentences.literal: Yet your subject's earnest sincerity also privately wishes Your Majesty in dwelling secure to think peril; do not say high-high above; constantly recall the meaning of overlooking the deep; not forget treading ice's warning.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet my stubborn heart begs you: feast in peace but taste peril—never murmur that you float too high—keep the cliff's lip and thin ice underfoot.

sentences.chinese: 盡除魏世之弊法，綏以新政之大化，使萬邦欣欣，喜戴洪惠，昆蟲草木，咸蒙恩澤。
sentences.literal: Exhaustively remove Wei age's harmful laws; pacify with new government's great transformation; cause myriad regions joyful-joyful, gladly bearing vast kindness; insects and plants all receive grace-moisture.
sentences.idiomatic: Scrub Wei's stale statutes, smooth the realm with fresh reform until every quarter laughs under broad favor—even weed and worm taste your rain.

sentences.chinese: 朝廷詠康哉之歌，山藪無伐檀之人，此固天下所視望者也。
sentences.literal: Court recites the Kang-zai song; mountains and marshes have none who fell sandalwood—this indeed is what All Under Heaven looks toward.
sentences.idiomatic: Let ministers hymn the "how peaceful" verse and leave hills free of sandalwood thieves—that is what the world cranes to see.

sentences.chinese: 陛下自初踐阼，發無諱之詔，置箴諫之官，赫然寵異諤諤之臣，以明好直言之信，恐陳事者知直言之不用，皆杜口結舌，祥瑞亦曷由來哉！
sentences.literal: Your Majesty from your first treading of the throne issued edicts without taboo, established remonstrance officials, brilliantly favored and distinguished outspoken ministers, to clarify faith in loving blunt speech—lest those who present affairs know blunt speech is not used, all seal mouths and tie tongues—how then would auspicious omens come!
sentences.idiomatic: From your first step on the throne you pledged blunt counsel, installed critic posts, and lifted noisy dissenters high—yet if speakers learn honesty buys silence, lips weld shut and omens lose their road to court.

sentences.chinese: 臣無陸生之才，不在顧問之地，蓋聞主聖臣直，義在於有犯無隱。
sentences.literal: Your subject lacks Master Lu's talent and is not in counsel's place; your subject has heard that when the lord is sage the ministers are straight—the righteousness lies in risking offense without concealment.
sentences.idiomatic: I am no Lu Jia; I do not sit in your advisory circle—yet they say a holy lord welcomes blunt servants: duty is to risk offense and hide nothing.

sentences.chinese: 臣不惟疏遠，未信而言，敢曆論前代隆名之君及亡敗之主廢興所由，又博陳舉賢之路，廣開養老之制，崇必信之道，又張設議者之難，凡五事以聞。
sentences.literal: Your subject not only is distant and estranged, untrusted yet speaking—dares serially discuss former generations' sovereigns of lofty fame and ruined defeated lords' rise-fall causes; again broadly presents paths for raising worthies, broadly opens systems for nurturing old age, exalts ways of certain faith; again spreads out debaters' difficulties—in all five matters to report.
sentences.idiomatic: Remote and never proven, I still presume to trace how famed kings rose and fallen tyrants sank; I widen roads for talent, broaden care for elders, lift honest dealing, and lay out what critics will fight—in five threads for your ear.

sentences.chinese: 臣之所言，皆直陳古今已行故事，非新聲異端也。
sentences.literal: What your subject speaks all bluntly states antiquity and today's already practiced precedents; it is not new tunes or heterodox doctrine.
sentences.idiomatic: Every line I offer walks worn grooves of old and recent precedent—no novelty, no heresy.

sentences.chinese: 辭義實淺，不足採納。
sentences.literal: The wording's meaning is truly shallow, insufficient to be adopted.
sentences.idiomatic: The phrasing stays shallow—hardly worth lifting wholesale.

sentences.chinese: 然臣私心，誠謂有可發起覺悟遺忘。
sentences.literal: Yet your subject's private heart truly says there is what can stir awakening of forgotten things.
sentences.idiomatic: Still I believe it may jog memory on points half sleeping.

sentences.chinese: 願陛下察臣愚忠，湣臣狂直，無使天下以言者為戒。
sentences.literal: May Your Majesty observe your subject's foolish loyalty, pity your subject's mad bluntness; do not cause All Under Heaven to take speakers as warning.
sentences.idiomatic: See my clumsy loyalty, pity my rash tongue—do not teach the realm that speech is peril.

sentences.chinese: 疾痛增篤，退念桑梓之詩，惟狐死之義，輒取長休，歸近墳墓。
sentences.literal: Your subject's illness and pain grew severe; recalling the mulberry-and-catalpa poem and the lesson that the fox faces its burial mound, your subject then took long rest, returning near tombs.
sentences.idiomatic: Pain gnaws deeper; I remember the ode of home and the fox who faces its mound—I claim long leave and crawl toward family graves.

sentences.chinese: 顧瞻宮闕，系情皇極，不勝丹款，遣息穎表言。
sentences.literal: Looking toward palace gate-towers, tying feeling to the august pole, unable to bear crimson sincerity—your subject sends his son Ying to memorialize speech.
sentences.idiomatic: Though my eyes cling to your towers and my heart locks on the throne, this honest ache overflows—so I send my son Ying to carry these words.

sentences.chinese: 其一曰：臣聞善有章也，著在經典；
sentences.literal: The first says: your subject has heard good has manifest regulation—it is written in classics;
sentences.idiomatic: First: I am told virtue wears bright badges—the canon says so;

sentences.chinese: 惡有罰也，戒在刑書。
sentences.literal: evil has punishment—it is warned in penal writings.
sentences.idiomatic: evil carries stripes—the statute scroll says so.

sentences.chinese: 上自遠古，下洎秦、漢，其明王霸主及亡國暗君，故可得而稱；
sentences.literal: Above from remote antiquity, below down to Qin and Han—their enlightened kings, hegemonic lords, and ruined-state dark sovereigns—thus can be named and cited;
sentences.idiomatic: From deepest antiquity down through Qin and Han, shining kings, league champions, and extinguished fools can still be named;

sentences.chinese: 至於忠蹇賢相及佞諂奸臣，亦可得而言。
sentences.literal: As for loyal obstructive worthy chancellors and flattery-murmuring treacherous ministers—also can be spoken of.
sentences.idiomatic: so can blunt loyal ministers and smiling traitors.

sentences.chinese: 故朝有諤諤盡規之臣，無不昌也；
sentences.literal: Therefore courts having outspoken exhaust-remonstrance ministers—none do not flourish;
sentences.idiomatic: Courts noisy with critics thrive;

sentences.chinese: 任用阿諛唯唯之士，無不亡也。
sentences.literal: employing fawning yes-yes gentlemen—none do not perish.
sentences.idiomatic: courts stuffed with nodding flatterers rot.

sentences.chinese: 是有國者皆欲求忠以自輔，舉賢以自佐；
sentences.literal: Therefore those who possess states all desire seeking loyalty to assist themselves, raising worthies to aid themselves;
sentences.idiomatic: Every holder of a realm claims to want loyal hands and worthy aides;

sentences.chinese: 而亡國破家者相繼，皆由任失其人。
sentences.literal: yet ruined-state broken-house ones succeed one another—all come from appointment losing the right men.
sentences.idiomatic: yet dynasties fall in rows because the wrong faces fill the chairs.

sentences.chinese: 所謂賢者不賢，忠者不忠也。
sentences.literal: What is called worthy is not worthy; what is called loyal is not loyal.
sentences.idiomatic: They praise worth yet seat mediocrity; cry loyalty yet harbor wolves.

sentences.chinese: 臣謹言前任賢所由興，任不肖所以亡者。
sentences.literal: Your subject respectfully speaks of former employing worthies' whereby rise, employing unworthies' whereby perishing.
sentences.idiomatic: Let me trace how wise appointments built thrones and foolish ones pulled them down.

sentences.chinese: 堯之末年，四凶在朝而不去，八元在家而不舉，然致天平地寧，四門穆穆，其功固在重華之為相。
sentences.literal: In Yao's late years, four villains were at court yet not removed; eight yuan were at home yet not raised—yet he brought Heaven flat and earth tranquil, four gates august-quiet—the achievement indeed lay in Chonghua's serving as minister.
sentences.idiomatic: Late Yao kept four monsters in hall and eight talents in obscurity—yet heaven steadied and gates grew solemn because Shun as minister steadied the helm.

sentences.chinese: 夏癸放於鳴條，商辛梟於牧野，此俱萬乘之主，而國滅身擒，由不能屬任賢相，用婦人之言，荒淫無道，肆志沈宴，作靡靡之樂，長夜之飲，於是登糟丘，臨酒池，觀牛飲，望肉林，龍逢忠而被害，比干諫而剖心，天下之所以歸惡者也。
sentences.literal: Xia Gui was banished at Mingtiao; Shang Xin was executed-and-displayed at Muye—these both were lords of ten thousand chariots, yet state extinguished and person captured—because they could not entrust succession to worthy chancellors, employed women's words, were dissolute without way, indulged will in sinking banquets, made dissolving-dissolving music, long-night drinking; thereupon ascended lees-mound, overlooked wine pool, watched ox-drinking, gazed on meat forest; Longfeng was loyal yet harmed, Bi Gan remonstrated yet heart cut out—this is why All Under Heaven turned evil toward them.
sentences.idiomatic: Jie fell at Mingtiao; Zhou's head answered Muye—both rode ten thousand chariots yet lost realm and liberty because they spurned wise ministers, obeyed women's whispers, drowned in lust and night-long cups, built hills of dregs and seas of wine, staged herd drinking under forests of meat—Longfeng died loyal, Bi Gan's heart was carved out for speaking—and the world learned to hate them.

sentences.chinese: 太甲暴虐，顛覆湯之典制，於是伊尹放之桐宮，而能改悔反善，三年而後歸於亳。
sentences.literal: Taijia was cruel and tyrannical, overturned Tang's statutes and systems; thereupon Yi Yin banished him to Tong Palace, and he was able to reform regret and return to good; after three years then returned to Bo.
sentences.idiomatic: Taijia shattered Tang's laws until Yi Yin locked him in Tong Palace—where shame turned him decent and three years later he reclaimed Bo.

sentences.chinese: 既已放而復還，殷道微而復興，諸侯咸服，號稱太宗，實賴阿衡之盡忠也。
sentences.literal: Already having been banished yet returning, Yin way faint yet reviving, feudal lords all submitted, titled Grand Ancestor—it truly depended on Ah Heng's exhausting loyalty.
sentences.idiomatic: Banished yet welcomed back, Yin rallied thin blood until lords bowed and histories crowned him Grand Ancestor—all credit to Yi Yin the Regent's stubborn faith.

sentences.chinese: 周室既衰，諸侯並爭，天王微弱，政遂陵遲。
sentences.literal: Zhou house already declined, feudal lords together contended; Heavenly King was weak slight; governance then slid downhill.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhou faded while barons clawed each other—the Son of Heaven shrank and government slid downhill.

sentences.chinese: 齊桓公，淫亂之主耳；
sentences.literal: Duke Huan of Qi—merely a dissolute-disorderly lord;
sentences.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi was a rake at heart;

sentences.chinese: 然所以能九合一匡之功，有尊周之名，誠管夷吾之力。
sentences.literal: Yet the reason he could achieve nine assemblies one rectification's merit, possess honoring Zhou's fame—truly was Guan Yiwu's strength.
sentences.idiomatic: yet nine leagues and one rescue of order, plus fame as Zhou's shield, rode wholly on Guan Zhong's spine.

sentences.chinese: 及其死也，蟲流出門，豈非任豎貂之過乎！
sentences.literal: When it came to his death, worms flowed out the gate—is it not fault of employing Shu Diao!
sentences.idiomatic: When he died maggots crawled from his hall—price of trusting Shu Diao!

sentences.chinese: 且一桓公之身，得管仲，其功如彼；
sentences.literal: Moreover one Duke Huan's person—obtaining Guan Zhong—his merit was like that;
sentences.idiomatic: One man named Huan with Guan Zhong wrought miracles;

sentences.chinese: 用豎貂，其亂如此。
sentences.literal: employing Shu Diao—his disorder was like this.
sentences.idiomatic: trust Shu Diao and rot sets in overnight.

sentences.chinese: 夫榮辱存亡，實在所任，可不審哉！
sentences.literal: Now glory-disgrace survival-perishing truly lie in whom one appoints—can one not examine!
sentences.idiomatic: Glory or ruin rides on your roster—choose with both eyes open!

sentences.chinese: 秦本伯翳之後，微微小邑，至秦仲始大，有車馬禮樂侍御之好焉。
sentences.literal: Qin originally was descendant of Boyi—a tiny petty town; reaching Duke Zhong of Qin it began great, having chariot-horse rites-music attendant-driver fondness therein.
sentences.idiomatic: Qin sprang from Boyi's blood as a flyspeck fort until Duke Zhong swelled it enough to fancy chariots, drums, and polished harness.

sentences.chinese: 自穆公至於始皇，皆能留心待賢，遠求異士，招由余於西戎，致五羖于宛市，取丕豹于晉鄉，迎蹇叔于宗裏。
sentences.literal: From Duke Mu down to First Emperor, all were able to fix heart on awaiting worthies, seek afar for unusual gentlemen—summoned You Yu from western Rong, brought five black rams at Wan market, took Pi Bao from Jin countryside, welcomed Jian Shu from Zong hamlet.
sentences.idiomatic: From Duke Mu to the First Emperor every lord hunted strangers with patience—You Yu from the western tribes, Baili Xi bought with five skins in Wan, Pi Bao stolen from Jin soil, Jian Shu coaxed from Zong lane.
